beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Swara Joshi, and this week on the Loon Conservation AI project, two things came together. Nikhil and I finished annotating every image currently available to us in CVAT, and I kept refining the researcher-facing prototype so its workflow matches the real tool we're building toward.

show.event: The cold open introduces the week's two converging tracks.

beats.narration_text: This week had a real through-line: finish annotating every image we currently have, and keep shaping the researcher-facing prototype so it matches the tool we're actually building. Two separate tracks, frontend and dataset, both moved from planning into structured, hands-on work, and both are converging toward the same eventual system.

show.event: Three layers stack the week's converging tracks.

props.sparkLine: Two tracks, moving toward one system.

layers.title: Complete the labeled dataset
layers.sub: Every currently available image annotated in CVAT with Nikhil

layers.title: Refine the researcher prototype

layers.title: Converge on one system

props.caption: Both sides of the project moved from planning into real, structured work this week.

beats.narration_text: Completing the annotations meant confronting real practical challenges: differences in object size, visibility, image quality, framing, lighting, reflections, and environmental conditions. Every one of those has to be handled consistently, because consistency across the dataset only gets more important as it grows.

show.event: A chip grid lists what consistent annotation requires.

props.caption: Every one of these becomes a labeling rule the dataset must hold to.

beats.narration_text: The process is simple to state: raw images go through annotation, become a labeled dataset, and eventually feed model training and detection. Completing this week's annotation work is the milestone that moves us from having raw images to having real, structured, labeled data, the necessary foundation before any model training can begin.

show.event: A source flow traces raw images to a labeled dataset.

props.sparkLine: From raw images to a labeled dataset.
props.destTitle: Where this data is eventually headed
props.arcCaption: Raw images become labeled data before any model ever sees them.
props.settleLine: The dataset is still small, but the path forward is mapped.

beats.narration_text: One real question follows from finishing this pass of annotation: is it time to start training a detection model? Not yet. The dataset is still relatively small, so the plan is to keep annotating and building before training and evaluating anything. A weak model trained too early would tell us less than no model at all.

beats.narration_text: On the interface side, the real work this week was thinking through how footage uploads, metadata, detections, observations, and verification will eventually connect. The prototype still isn't wired to a real computer-vision model, but it's already useful for spotting where the researcher experience needs to change.

show.event: A chip grid lists how the interface pieces connect.

props.sparkLine: How the pieces connect in the interface
props.caption: The frontend is being shaped around how these pieces connect, not just how they look.

beats.narration_text: So the honest state: we don't have a trained model, and the dataset is still relatively small. But finishing the annotation of every currently available image is a real milestone. It moves this project from raw images to structured, labeled data, with the prototype's workflow shaped to match.

show.event: A verdict artifact summarizes the honest state of the project.

artifactLines: Nikhil and I finished annotating every image currently available to us in CVAT.
That work moves the project from raw images to a real, structured labeled dataset.
The researcher prototype is more representative of the intended workflow, but still not connected to a real model.
The dataset stays small for now; the next phase is building it further before training begins.

beats.narration_text: Next, I'll keep building the dataset as more footage becomes available, and keep refining the frontend based on feedback from the National Loon Center and Nikhil. Once there's enough loon-specific data, the next real step is experimenting with detection and counting. If you want to help, here's one question: what's the clearest sign that a dataset is finally big and varied enough to start training on?

show.event: The handoff composer presents the next-step prompt.

beats.narration_text: That's the update for this week. Thank you for watching, and I'll see you in the next one.
